requirement: The getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.install.symposium.skill_hook` says: "The getting-started documentation MUST explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill." This clause only constrains what the documentation says. It does not prescribe a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface.

I considered whether the clause could be a structural obligation, such as a requirement that the explanation live in a particular file or section. The text doesn't say that. Any wording or location in the getting-started docs that conveys the same fact satisfies it. So the obligation is purely about observable content, and no implementation root is needed.

The supplied roots are `md/getting_started.md#section[Getting%20started]/paragraph@1bfd8400968e` and `README.md`. The first holds only `{impl}` markers for this requirement and its parent. The second is a README outline. Neither is required to carry structural evidence. Whether the docs really say this is a behavioral or content matter, so it is outside this structural criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation. The getting-started documentation must explain that the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill. It names no other conditions.

Two tests carry a `{test}` reference to `requirements.install.symposium.skill_hook`. Both loop over `README.md` and `md/getting_started.md`, so each getting-started document is checked.

- `tests/repository.rs#fn[getting_started_documents_symposium_setup_and_skill_migration]` asserts the words `session`, `hook` and `` `habeas` skill `` appear in each file. It then asserts that a single normalized paragraph contains `hook tells`, `load the `habeas` skill before starting any work` and `session`. That ties the hook, the instruction to load the skill, and the session-start context together.
- `tests/repository.rs#fn[installation_guides_cover_setup_hooks_refresh_and_preserving_local_skills]` asserts both files contain `load the `habeas` skill`. It also asserts the exact README sentence and the exact guide sentence saying the session-start hook tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill before starting any work.

A document that omitted or misstated the hook's instruction to load the skill would fail these assertions. The other assertions in these tests, covering setup advice, refresh and preserving local edits, belong to other obligations. They are not part of this requirement.

I found no behavioral gap and no marking gap.
